brief.label: US band and radio rules
brief.text: UHF RFID in the United States operates at 902-928 MHz under FCC Part 15.247 (47 CFR 15.247): up to 1 W conducted output / 4 W EIRP with a 6 dBi antenna, frequency hopping across at least 50 channels. Readers carry the FCC certification; passive tags must be antenna-tuned for the band. EU-tuned 865-868 MHz inlays underperform in US portals.

brief.label: Federal procurement fit
brief.text: NDAA Section 889 (FAR 52.204-25) bars covered telecom/video-surveillance equipment from five named manufacturers — Proud Tek is not one, and passive tags and cards cannot route or redirect user data. Trade Agreements Act: China is not a designated country under FAR Part 25, so China-origin end products generally cannot be sold on TAA-covered contracts such as GSA Schedules.

brief.label: Landed cost
brief.text: Most RFID cards and tags enter the US under HTS 8523.52.00 ("smart cards"), general duty rate Free; China-origin goods add 25% under Section 301 List 3 (heading 9903.88.03). Proud Tek DDP quotes include duty, tariff, and brokerage, so the quoted price is the landed price.

sections.title: Get the band right: 902-928 MHz under FCC Part 15
sections.intro: The most expensive mistake in cross-border RFID sourcing is band mismatch. US UHF runs at 902-928 MHz under FCC Part 15.247; Europe's workhorse band is 865-868 MHz. An inlay tuned for Frankfurt performs beautifully in Frankfurt and sulks in a Fresno dock door — radio physics does not read purchase orders. New to frequency planning? Start with our [LF vs HF vs UHF guide](/blog/rfid-frequencies-lf-hf-uhf-explained/).

faq.question: Are your UHF RFID products FCC-compliant for use in the United States?
faq.answer: Yes. Our UHF RFID tags and labels are designed for the 902-928 MHz frequency band as required by FCC Part 15 for unlicensed UHF RFID devices in the United States. We use chips (Impinj Monza, NXP UCODE) that are fully characterized for the US frequency band and can provide compliance documentation upon request.

faq.question: Do passive RFID tags need their own FCC certification?
faq.answer: No. Under FCC Part 15 the certification obligation sits with the reader — the intentional radiator — which must carry an FCC ID. Passive UHF tags are not transmitters; they backscatter the reader's signal, so what matters is that the tag antenna is tuned for the US 902-928 MHz band. When evaluating suppliers, ask for the reader's FCC ID and the tag's tuning and performance data rather than a certificate for the tag itself.

faq.question: How do tariffs and import duties affect pricing for US buyers?
faq.answer: We offer DDP pricing that includes all applicable import duties, customs brokerage fees, and tariff costs in the quoted price. This gives US buyers a fully landed cost with no surprise charges. Our logistics team is experienced with US import regulations and HTS classification for RFID products.

faq.question: What Incoterms can US buyers choose?
faq.answer: US buyers can order EXW Shenzhen, FOB Shenzhen/Yantian, or DDP to door. Most US customers choose DDP: the quote includes freight, US import duty, Section 301 tariff, and customs brokerage, so the quoted price is the landed price. EXW and FOB suit buyers running their own freight programs or consolidated sea shipments.

faq.question: Can I resell your products on a GSA Schedule or other TAA-covered federal contract?
faq.answer: Generally no for China-origin end products: the Trade Agreements Act requires designated-country end products on TAA-covered procurements, and China is not a designated country under FAR Part 25. Commercial and open-market purchases are a separate analysis. NDAA Section 889 is a different rule — it bars covered equipment from five named manufacturers; Proud Tek is not among them, and passive tags and cards cannot route or redirect user data. For a specific solicitation, have your contracts counsel review the clauses.

faq.question: Can I get product samples before placing a large order?
faq.answer: Yes. We provide free sample kits including RFID cards, tags, labels, and wristbands shipped via DHL express to any US address at no charge. Samples typically arrive within 5-7 business days. Custom-printed samples with your artwork are also available with a 7-10 day lead time.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for US buyers?
faq.answer: MOQs for US orders match our standard factory minimums: custom-printed PVC cards start at 500 pieces (digital printing accepts runs as low as 100), NFC inlays and labels at 1,000 pieces (one roll), and silicone wristbands at 500 pieces. Recurring production programs typically run 1,000-5,000 pieces per SKU.
